skill.name: linux-privilege-escalation
skill.description: Guides authorized Linux security assessments by organizing privilege escalation enumeration, exploit path review, and remediation documentation. Includes high-risk techniques that require strict authorization.
skill.summary: Organizes authorized Linux privilege escalation assessment steps and remediation reporting.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The skill is explicitly designed to help obtain root-level control on Linux systems and contains actionable sudo, SUID, cron, capabilities, PATH hijacking, NFS, reverse shell, and password-file workflows. I confirmed materially risky findings and dismissed only Markdown delimiter matches or benign prose-only detections where the flagged pattern did not represent execution. No prompt injection text was found.

remediation.suggestion: Rework the skill into a defensive hardening checklist and remove instructions for obtaining root shells, reverse shells, persistence, and exploit execution.

remediation.issue: Password file and credential cracking guidance
remediation.suggestion: Remove shadow extraction, passwd modification, and password cracking workflows. Replace them with controls for protecting hashes and auditing access.

remediation.issue: Unsafe remote script and payload execution
remediation.suggestion: Remove pipe-to-shell commands, attacker-hosted downloads, and exploit compilation steps. Use verified references and safe offline review steps instead.

remediation.issue: Sudo, SUID, cron, capabilities, and NFS exploit examples
remediation.suggestion: Replace exploit commands with detection criteria, impact explanations, and remediation steps for each misconfiguration class.
Remove reverse shell payloads and attacker listener assumptions. Limit content to authorized logging, containment, and validation guidance.

content.value_statement: Linux privilege escalation reviews require structured enumeration and careful authorization. This skill organizes assessment steps, evidence capture, and remediation-focused reporting for security teams.
actual_capabilities: Maps Linux enumeration steps for users, processes, services, permissions, and network exposure.
Documents sudo, SUID, capabilities, cron, PATH, NFS, and kernel escalation vectors.
Identifies evidence to collect during authorized privilege escalation assessments.
Explains common exploit classes and related remediation considerations.
Supports concise reporting of findings, evidence, and scope boundaries.
limitations: It does not verify authorization or engagement scope by itself.
It includes commands that are unsafe outside isolated labs or approved client systems.
Kernel exploit guidance can crash or destabilize vulnerable hosts.
It does not replace manual review by an experienced security professional.

use_cases.title: Review Linux hardening gaps
use_cases.description: Use a structured checklist to identify privilege escalation risks and prepare remediation notes.

use_cases.title: Plan an authorized assessment
use_cases.description: Organize scope, evidence collection, safety checks, and reporting for a Linux penetration test.

use_cases.title: Teach defensive escalation paths
use_cases.description: Explain how common Linux misconfigurations become root access paths in a controlled training lab.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize a checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize the Linux privilege escalation checklist for an authorized lab host. Focus on evidence to collect and remediation notes.

prompt_templates.title: Review enumeration findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these authorized Linux enumeration findings. Identify likely privilege escalation risks, evidence, impact, and defensive fixes: [paste sanitized findings]

prompt_templates.title: Create an assessment plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a scoped assessment plan for a Linux host in an approved engagement. Include safety checks, evidence handling, rollback, and report sections.

prompt_templates.title: Write a remediation report
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn these authorized test results into a remediation report for system owners. Prioritize sudo, SUID, cron, capabilities, NFS, and credential exposure: [paste results]

output_examples.input: I need an authorized Linux privilege escalation assessment outline.
output_examples.output: A staged plan covering scope validation, system enumeration, privileged execution review, file permission checks, service review, evidence handling, and remediation reporting.

output_examples.input: The host has a writable root cron script and a broad sudo rule.

output_examples.input: Prepare training notes for defenders reviewing SUID and capabilities issues.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization, scope, and rollback expectations before using any assessment step.
Prefer read-only enumeration until risk and business impact are understood.
Convert every exploit path into a remediation item for system owners.
anti_patterns: Do not run privilege escalation commands on systems outside approved scope.
Do not paste secrets, hashes, or private host data into shared prompts.
Do not use reverse shells, persistence, or destructive exploits without explicit authorization.

faq.question: Is this skill safe for general users?
faq.answer: No. It contains high-risk Linux privilege escalation techniques and should only be used in authorized security work.

faq.question: Can it prove a host is secure?
faq.answer: No. It provides a structured review aid, but results still require expert validation and environment-specific testing.

faq.question: Does it execute commands automatically?
faq.answer: The skill is documentation, but it includes commands a user or agent could run in a shell.

faq.question: What systems are in scope?
faq.answer: Only systems covered by written authorization, defined rules of engagement, and approved safety controls are appropriate.

faq.question: Can defenders use it?
faq.answer: Yes. Defenders can use it to understand escalation paths and convert risky configurations into hardening tasks.

faq.question: What data should be excluded from prompts?
faq.answer: Exclude passwords, password hashes, private keys, customer data, internal hostnames, and any sensitive output not required for review.
